A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S3OD research. All 17 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, ablations, synthetic-data quality measurements and efficiency results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds camouflage-detection experiments, expanded comparisons, feature analyses and decoder-regularization ablations.

M1.justification: The architecture, feature fusion, losses, mask selection and iterative weighting remain unchanged. However, the reported generation prompt changes from requiring complex backgrounds to mixing simple and complex scenes, with revised scene-variation instructions (v1 Figure 5; v2 Figure 11). This revises a method input without establishing that the dataset was regenerated.

E1.justification: v2 adds dedicated camouflaged-object detection on COD10K, CAMO and NC4K, including fine-tuning on CAMO and COD10K training sets (Section 5.5). This substantially extends task coverage to detecting foreground objects that blend into their backgrounds. The original DIS/SOD benchmarks and 139,981-image synthetic dataset remain.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluated comparators: FSPNet in Table 6; SAM, Pi-SAM and DIS-SAM in Table 13; and additional SOD/DIS methods including LDF, HRSOD, DHQ, PGNet, BASNet, U2Net, IS-Net, FP-DIS and UDUN in Table 14. Original comparisons remain. HQ-SAM and SAM-HQ denote the same comparator, not separate additions.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot COD transfer and COD fine-tuning, training BiRefNet and MVANet on S3OD (Table 3), expanded real-only training controls (Table 14), and regularization/decay configurations with diversity metrics (Table 15). Figure 8 adds generative precision-recall and UMAP assessments. The original DIS/SOD evaluation metrics and matched 10,000-image synthetic-data comparison remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's modality, backbone, mask-count, generation-round and prompting ablations, v2 adds feature-complementarity case analyses (Appendix A), image/mask domain-gap analyses (Appendix C), controls testing dataset benefits across architectures, and auxiliary-loss sensitivity tests examining branch collapse and diversity (Appendix G). These address substantial additional analytical questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, run-to-run variability or significance tests. The new entropy and average-IoU measurements describe prediction-branch diversity, not uncertainty in estimated experimental performance.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation values are retained, while v2 adds extensive results. Table 6 newly reports fine-tuned COD10K F-measure of 0.911 versus BiRefNet's 0.888, rather than a same-setting improvement over v1. New Table 13 also reports HQ-SAM overall F-measure of 0.859, versus 0.850 for SAM-HQ in retained Table 4, without explaining the evaluation difference.

T1.justification: The explicit model, objective and sampling equations are retained. Appendix G invokes the existing MHP/Voronoi interpretation to motivate the unchanged decaying auxiliary loss, but introduces no new formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: large-scale synthetic supervision, complementary generative/discriminative features, feedback-driven generation, ambiguity-aware prediction and strong DIS/HR-SOD generalization. The added experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds detailed interpretations of feature failures and complementarity, connects distribution coverage to generalization, and discusses performance relative to SAM adaptations. Appendix G explains regularization through branch collapse and sparse ambiguity. Appendix H newly discusses synthetic-data evaluation boundaries and computational limitations, extending v1's narrower quality and generalization discussion.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the mask decoder's real-data supervision, identifies ImageNet taxonomy as the category source, clarifies 25,000 images in each later generation round, and discloses the absence of a synthetic test split. It also adds a four-A6000, 2.5-day training alternative. These improve documentation without establishing changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature supporting COD benchmarks, additional segmentation baselines, SAM adaptations, UMAP and generative precision-recall analysis. Appendix F extends positioning against foundation-model adaptations, particularly DIS-SAM. The main related-work argument and novelty positioning in Section 2 remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits prose throughout, introduces S3ODNet naming, revises the prompting text, shortens its example list and updates headers and acknowledgments. Added experimental and appendix subsections extend the document, while the original main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds COD predictions, feature visualizations and a four-panel domain-gap figure (Figures 5, 6 and 8), plus Tables 3, 6 and 13–15. Existing qualitative figures are retained and relocated, the prompt box is revised and moved, and table placement is reorganized. These substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central empirical case: Table 3 tests S3OD with other architectures, addressing v1's limited separation of dataset and model benefits. COD transfer tests and decoder-regularization analyses also examine important previously unsupported aspects of generalization and ambiguity handling. These gains outweigh the added reporting weaknesses, including unexplained HQ-SAM score differences; run-level uncertainty remains absent.
